body: **Foco:** Comunicação integrada: Comunicação intercultural.
**Expressões:** To put it into perspective….
**Pronúncia:** Organização da informação pela entonação.
**22 palavras novas** (comunicação intercultural).
**Texto do dia:** blog, diário, crônica.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo integrar leitura, fala e escrita sobre equipes remotas e usar To put it into perspective…

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Blog: Working Across Time Zones
paras: Our team spans five time zones, and **the coordination of meetings** is a daily puzzle. **Having tried** several schedules, we now rotate the inconvenient hour so that no one **always** attends at midnight.

**To put it into perspective**, a single weekly meeting at 8 p.m. may seem minor, but over a year it adds up to nearly fifty evenings. We are **inclined to think** that fairness matters more than convenience.

The **adoption** of shared notes has also helped. Colleagues who cannot attend can **elaborate** on the discussion in writing, and **the avoidance of surprises** has reduced tension. It is not perfect, but **the improvement** is clear.

items.q: The team works in five time zones.
The same person always attends the midnight meeting.
The writer thinks convenience matters more than fairness.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence blog paragraph about working or studying across cultures, using at least three structures from the unit.
blocks.model: Having studied with classmates from four countries, I learned to ask questions twice. The adoption of shared notes improved our results. I am inclined to think that patience matters more than talent. To put it into perspective, one clear email saved us a week of confusion. Could I elaborate? Of course: clarity is respect.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
